name: Ruler Lab
mechanic: The child drags a ruler so its zero-end lines up with the start of an object, then taps the number on the ruler where the object ends to read its length. Tools snap-aligned but the child decides the reading.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is reveal-grid (tap to uncover), but here the CORE is physically positioning a measuring tool and reading a scale, not uncovering a hidden cell. Separation: the answer lives on a continuous scale the child reads, not a discrete grid cell.
fun_no_competition: the satisfying click as the ruler snaps to zero and the glowing number where the object's tip lands — 'so THAT's how long it is!'
character_world: a tiny inventor's workbench where curious critters bring odd objects (a pencil, a worm, a leaf) to be measured
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — draggable ruler sprite over a backdrop, scale ticks as DOM, tap-to-read
asset_idea: stub: gray ruler bar + numbered ticks + 6 object silhouettes; CA5: wooden ruler with brass ends, hand-drawn objects with measurable tips

name: Unit-Train Lay-Down
mechanic: The child drags identical unit-blocks (paper clips, cubes) end-to-end along an object until the object is fully covered, then counts the units laid to report the length. The experiment is figuring out how many units fit with no gaps or overlaps.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is build-a-world (place objects freely), but here placement is constrained to a measuring purpose — units MUST abut with no gaps. Separation from Ruler Lab: no pre-marked scale; the child constructs the unit count by iterating identical objects.
fun_no_competition: the snap of each clip butting against the last, and the count climbing — 'it's six paper clips long!'
character_world: a busy little ant crew laying a road of blocks across the garden
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — drag clones of a unit sprite with end-snap to the previous unit
asset_idea: stub: colored squares + object outline; CA5: chunky paper clips / wooden cubes with a friendly ant foreman

name: Estimate-Then-Reveal Jar
mechanic: A jar of objects is shown; the child first taps an estimate on a number-line slider (no counting allowed yet), THEN taps 'reveal' to count the items one-by-one as they hop out, comparing guess to actual. The skill is committing a reasoned guess before verifying.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is pop-the-right-ones, but nothing is 'wrong' here — the core is the predict-then-check loop: a committed estimate followed by a verified count. Separation: estimate-first sequencing is the mechanic, not selection.
fun_no_competition: the gleeful 'how close was I?' reveal as candies hop out and the guess-marker and count-marker meet on the line
character_world: a wondering owl who loves guessing jars at a sweet shop
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — slider DOM + sequential reveal animation of sprite instances
asset_idea: stub: glass jar + dots + horizontal slider; CA5: candy jar, hopping jellybeans, owl with a monocle

name: Balance Discoverer
mechanic: Two pans of a balance scale; the child loads an object onto each pan and watches the beam tip, discovering which is heavier by which side sinks. They can swap and re-test combinations until they can answer 'heavier / lighter'.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is sort-home (place items by category), but here placement is a TEST whose physical result (tipping) reveals the answer — the child experiments to discover weight order, not sort by a known label. Separation: the apparatus produces the verdict, not the child's prior knowledge.
fun_no_competition: the slow tilt of the beam and the 'clunk' — the apple wins! — pure cause-and-effect delight with no wrong move
character_world: a fruit-bat shopkeeper weighing produce on an old market scale
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — CSS rotation of the beam keyed to a per-object weight value; drag objects to pans
asset_idea: stub: two pans + pivot beam + weighted objects; CA5: brass market scale, ripe fruit, bat in an apron

name: Pour-to-the-Line
mechanic: The child tilts/taps a pitcher to pour liquid into a graduated container, stopping at a target fill-line shown on the side. They tune the pour to hit the marked level, reading the scale to know when to stop.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is grow-tend (nurture over time), but the core here is calibrating a continuous quantity to a target reading on a measuring vessel — capacity, not growth. Separation: a measurable target line and a controllable pour, a tune-to-target loop.
fun_no_competition: the rising liquid and the 'just right!' chime when it reaches the line — gentle no-spill tinkering
character_world: a friendly frog mixing pond-juice in a measuring cup
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — fill-bar height driven by hold duration, target line as DOM marker
asset_idea: stub: beaker + fill rectangle + target line; CA5: measuring cup with painted gradations, dripping pitcher, frog barista

name: Which Holds More?
mechanic: Two differently-shaped containers; the child fills one, pours its contents into the other, and discovers whether it overflows, exactly fills, or leaves room — testing capacity directly rather than judging by appearance (tall-skinny vs short-wide).
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is Pour-to-the-Line, but there the goal is hitting a line; here the goal is a COMPARISON discovered by transfer — does it overflow or not? Separation: the experiment is conservation-of-volume across shapes, surprising the eye.
fun_no_competition: the surprise — 'the skinny tall one held MORE?!' — overturning the look-bigger trap with a fun pour
character_world: a tea-party hedgehog testing which cup holds the most cocoa
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — fixed per-container capacity values; animate transfer and overflow
asset_idea: stub: two container outlines + liquid fill; CA5: mismatched whimsical teacups, steam, cozy hedgehog

name: Tune-the-Dial Number
mechanic: A dial/knob controls a big readout; the child rotates the dial until the displayed number matches a target shown by a character ('I want 7!'). Turning past or under is fine — they tune toward the value and watch it count up/down.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is magic-machine (input→transformed output), but no transformation happens — the dial IS the value and the child calibrates a continuous control to a target. Separation: tune-a-setting-to-a-target, not feed-and-transform.
fun_no_competition: the click-click of the dial and the readout flipping like an odometer until it locks green at the target
character_world: a robot DJ who requests numbers on a glowing console
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — rotary drag → angle → integer mapping, flip-clock readout in DOM
asset_idea: stub: knob + 7-seg display + target chip; CA5: retro radio dial, neon readout, boogie robot

name: Thermometer Reader
mechanic: A thermometer rises; the child reads the marked scale and taps the matching temperature (or drags a marker to where the mercury tops out). Variant: set the dial so the bath/oven reaches the 'just right' zone.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is Ruler Lab (read a linear scale), but a thermometer is a vertical scale tied to a sensed state (warm/cold) and supports a set-to-target sub-mode. Separation: vertical scale + thermal context, distinct affordance and number-line tie.
fun_no_competition: the mercury climbing and a 'just right' band glowing — porridge-not-too-hot satisfaction
character_world: a bear cub checking the temperature of three bowls of soup
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — vertical fill bar with tick scale, tap-to-read or drag marker
asset_idea: stub: vertical thermometer + ticks + marker; CA5: round-bulb thermometer, steamy soup bowls, sleepy bear

name: Estimate-the-Length Snap
mechanic: An object appears; the child first drags a 'guess marker' along a number-line to estimate its length in units, commits, THEN a ruler slides in to reveal the true length. They compare guess vs measured and see how close they got.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is Estimate-Then-Reveal Jar (estimate quantity), but here the estimate is a continuous LENGTH on a measurement scale, then verified by an actual measuring tool. Separation: length-estimation domain + ruler verification, not discrete count.
fun_no_competition: the reveal animation where the ruler glides in and your guess-flag and the true-mark sit side by side — 'only one off!'
character_world: a tailor mouse eyeballing ribbon before measuring it
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — estimate slider, then animate ruler overlay; compare two markers
asset_idea: stub: object + estimate slider + sliding ruler; CA5: spool of ribbon, measuring tape, mouse with pins

name: Combo Mixer Test
mechanic: The child mixes two color/ingredient inputs and observes the result, testing combinations to discover which pairs make the target (blue+yellow→green). Free no-fail experimentation until they find the combo the character wants, with a record strip of what they've tried.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is magic-machine (single input transformed), but here the child TESTS multiple combinations and the discovery is which combination produces an effect — a hypothesis-testing sandbox, plus an emergent data record. Separation: combinatorial test loop, not a fixed transform.
fun_no_competition: the pop and swirl when two things mix — 'whoa, that made orange!' — endless safe what-if tinkering
character_world: a paint-splattered octopus chemist in a bubbling lab
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — fixed combination lookup table, swatch reveal, tried-list as DOM chips
asset_idea: stub: two input slots + result swatch + tried row; CA5: beakers, color splashes, goggled octopus

name: Number-Line Hop Predictor
mechanic: A frog sits on a number line; the child predicts where it lands after a stated hop ('hop forward 3'), drags a prediction marker, then taps 'hop' to watch the frog jump and verify. Tunes their sense of position and jumps.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is path-journey (move along a path), but path-journey is travel/narrative; here the core is PREDICTING a landing position on a numbered scale and checking, a measurement/number-line reading skill. Separation: predict-the-coordinate then verify, not traverse.
fun_no_competition: the suspense of the predicted spot then the frog's 'boing boing boing' landing exactly (or near) your marker
character_world: a leapfrog on lily-pad number stones across a pond
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — number-line DOM, draggable marker, hop animation by translate
asset_idea: stub: number line + frog sprite + marker; CA5: lily-pad stones with numerals, splashy frog

name: Tally Tester Spinner
mechanic: The child spins/taps a spinner many times and records each result into a tally chart, discovering through repeated trials which outcome comes up most. The experiment generates data the child reads off the chart.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is sticker-album (collect into slots), but here the slot-filling is DATA collection from repeated trials and the payoff is reading 'which has the most' off the chart — represent-and-interpret data, not collection-completion. Separation: trial→record→interpret, an experiment producing a dataset.
fun_no_competition: the random spin and the tally marks stacking up — 'star is winning the chart!' — discovery without a clock
character_world: a carnival raccoon running a friendly prize wheel
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — randomized spinner, accumulate counts into a DOM bar/tally chart
asset_idea: stub: spinner wheel + tally rows; CA5: carnival wheel with icons, chalkboard tally, raccoon barker

name: Shadow-Length Clock Lab
mechanic: The child drags the sun across the sky and watches a stick's shadow grow and shrink; they then measure the shadow with a unit-ruler at different sun positions, discovering the relationship by testing. A measure-as-you-experiment sandbox.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is Ruler Lab (measure a thing), but the thing here CHANGES as the child manipulates a variable (sun position), so it's an experiment about how an input affects a measurable output. Separation: set-a-variable-and-measure-the-effect loop.
fun_no_competition: swooshing the sun and watching the shadow stretch like taffy, then catching its length with the ruler — 'longest at sunset!'
character_world: a meerkat scientist on a sunny dune with a measuring stick
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — sun position drives shadow width via simple formula; reuse ruler component
asset_idea: stub: sun slider + stick + shadow rect + ruler; CA5: desert dune, long warm shadows, goggled meerkat

name: Order-the-Lengths Bench
mechanic: Several objects of different lengths are scattered; the child measures each (with a ruler or unit-blocks), records the lengths, then drags the objects into order shortest-to-longest, using the MEASURED values rather than eyeballing.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is Order-by-measure ideas like Balance Discoverer (compare two), but here the child measures THREE+ objects and orders them by recorded length — measure-then-seriate. Separation: multi-object ordering grounded in own measurements, an indirect-comparison skill.
fun_no_competition: the lineup snapping into a neat staircase once everything's measured — tidy 'now they're in order!' satisfaction
character_world: a carpenter beaver sorting planks by length on a workbench
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — measure each via ruler component, store values, drag-reorder slots
asset_idea: stub: 3-4 bars + ruler + order tray; CA5: wooden planks of varied length, sawdust, hard-hat beaver

name: Read-the-Diagram Detective (ELA)
mechanic: An informational diagram (a labeled bug, a plant, a machine) is shown; a question asks 'find the part that does X' and the child taps the labeled part, using the diagram's labels and the caption to discover the answer. They test taps and read to confirm.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is i-spy-scene (find an item visually), but here the find is driven by READING informational labels/captions to identify a part by its function — a use-text-features comprehension skill, not visual search. Separation: text-feature reading is the tool, the diagram is the data.
fun_no_competition: the 'aha, the wings are for flying!' as the right label lights up — feels like real science detective work
character_world: a magnifying-glass-toting ladybug naturalist labeling specimens
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — labeled hotspots over a diagram image, caption text in DOM
asset_idea: stub: diagram image + label callouts + caption box; CA5: storybook nature diagram, leader lines, ladybug detective

name: Estimate-the-Distance Drop
mechanic: A character must reach a target; the child estimates how many unit-steps away it is, drags a 'this far' bracket, commits, then steps the character one unit at a time to verify the distance. Predict the span, then count to check.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is Number-Line Hop Predictor (predict a landing), but here the child estimates a SPAN/distance between two points and verifies by iterating units, an estimation-of-length-in-units skill. Separation: span estimation + unit-iteration verify, not single landing position.
fun_no_competition: guessing 'about 5 steps?' then the little walk that lands right on the target — close-guess celebration with zero penalty
character_world: a puppy hopping stepping-stones to reach its bone
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — draggable span bracket on a unit track, then step animation
asset_idea: stub: start + target + unit track + bracket; CA5: garden path stones, eager puppy, buried bone
